name: Using Date filtering
markdown:
# Smart Search

[](#smart-search)

## Date filtering

[](#date-filtering)

### `date_query`

[](#date_query)

Filter based on date.

Parameters

array $wp\_date\_queries: An array of date queries. See [WP\_Date\_Query](https://developer.wordpress.org/reference/classes/wp_date_query/). Each query can contain the following keys:

-   relation (optional): The logical relation between queries (AND or OR). Default is AND.
-   year
-   month
-   day
-   hour (optional)
-   minute (optional)
-   second (optional)
-   before (optional): A date or array specifying the upper bound of the date range.
-   after (optional): A date or array specifying the lower bound of the date range.
-   inclusive (optional): A boolean indicating whether the date range is inclusive. Default is true.
-   comparison (optional): Accepts ‘=’, ‘!=’, ‘>’, ‘>=’, ‘<’, ‘<=’. Default ‘=’. Currently we do not support ‘IN’, ‘BETWEEN’, ‘NOT IN’ and ‘NOT BETWEEN’.

#### Description

[](#description)

This filter prevents posts and pages outside the date ranges from being returned. WPE Smart Search respects these date filters.

#### Examples

[](#examples)

You would want to only show posts from `1/1/2021` OR before `2024-01-13` inclusive OR before `2023-12-12` at exactly `12:12:12`.

The following arrays can be built with this [WP\_Date\_Query Generator](https://generatewp.com/wp_date_query/).

```
add_action( 'pre_get_posts', function( $query ) {  // Ensure this only modifies the main query on the front-end.  if ( ! is_admin() && $query->is_main_query() && $query->is_search() ) {    // Set up date query arguments.    $date_query_args = array(      'relation' => 'OR',      array(        'year'    => 2021,        'month'   => 1,        'day'     => 1,        'compare' => '=',      ),      array(        'before'    => '2024-01-13',        'inclusive' => true,      ),      array(        'year'    => 2023,        'month'   => 12,        'day'     => 12,        'hour'    => 12,        'minute'  => 12,        'second'  => 12,        'compare' => '<',      ),    );    // Apply the date query to the main query.    $query->set( 'date_query', $date_query_args );  }});
```

name: Using Hooks and Filters
markdown:
# Smart Search

[](#smart-search)

## Hooks and Filters

[](#hooks-and-filters)

### `wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields`

[](#wpe_smartsearchextra_fields)

Filters the post fields before indexing.

```
apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields', string $data, WP_Post $post )
```

#### Description

[](#description)

Use this filter to add or remove fields before an object is indexed.

#### Parameters

[](#parameters)

```
$data array
```

Contains all of the data before indexing.

```
$post WP_Post
```

The current post object being indexed.

#### Examples

[](#examples)

Adding a custom field.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields',    function( array $data, WP_Post $post ) {        $data['custom-field'] = 'custom field test';        return $data;    },    10,    2);
```

Adding the post permalink.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields',    function( array $data, WP_Post $post ) {        //sample value http://localhost:8000/hello-world        $data['url'] = get_permalink($post);        return $data;    },    10,    2);
```

Adding the post locale with a language plugin, i.e. `polylang`

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields',    function( array $data, WP_Post $post ) {        //sample values EN | ES        $data['locale'] = pll_get_post_language($post->ID);        return $data;    },    10,    2);
```

### `wpe_smartsearch/extra_search_config_fields`

[](#wpe_smartsearchextra_search_config_fields)

Filters the search config fields.

```
apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/extra_search_config_fields', array $fields, string $post_type )
```

#### Description

[](#description-1)

Use this filter to add or remove fields to the Search Config.

#### Parameters

[](#parameters-1)

```
$fields array
```

Contains all of the search config fields for the given `$post_type`.

```
$post WP_Post
```

The current post\_type being processed for Search Config fields.

#### Examples

[](#examples-1)

Adding a custom search config field.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/extra_search_config_fields',    function ( $fields, $post_type ) {        if ($post_type === 'post' ) {            $fields[] = 'my-custom-field';        }
        return $fields;    },    10,    2);
```

Note

This hook will run multiple times for each post type that exists.

The following search config field will get added to all post types.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/extra_search_config_fields',    function ( $fields, $post_type ) {        $fields[] = 'all-post-types-custom-field';        return $fields;    },    10,    2);
```

### `wpe_smartsearch/excluded_post_types`

[](#wpe_smartsearchexcluded_post_types)

Filters the post types ban list.

```
apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/excluded_post_types' );
```

#### Description

[](#description-2)

Filters a list of post types that won’t be considered for WP Engine Smart Search

#### Examples

[](#examples-2)

```
add_filter(    'wpe_smartsearch/excluded_post_types',    function (  ) {        return array(            'zombie',            'rabbit',            'page'        );    },    10,    2);
```

### `wpe_smartsearch/search/facet_blocks_enabled`

[](#wpe_smartsearchsearchfacet_blocks_enabled)

Enables or disables WPE Engine Smart Search search-related Facets.

```
apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/search/facet_blocks_enabled', true )
```

#### Description

[](#description-3)

This filter enables or disables the search-related Facet Blocks provided by WP Engine Smart Search. They are enabled by default. It would be useful to disable them if you are not using them, or if there is a conflict with your custom facets, theme or plugin.

#### Examples

[](#examples-3)

Disabling WPE Engine Smart Search Facets.

```
add_filter( 'wpe_smartsearch/search/facet_blocks_enabled', '__return_false' );
```

### `wpe_smartsearch/acf/excluded_field_names`

[](#wpe_smartsearchacfexcluded_field_names)

Filter ACF fields from being indexed to WPE Engine Smart Search.

```
$excluded_field_names = apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/acf/excluded_field_names', array() );
```

#### Description

[](#description-4)

This filter prevents ACF fields to be indexed using the field name. This is very useful for a number of reasons:

-   Preventing unnecessary data from being indexed, increases performance.
-   Prevents errors from being thrown when indexing data ( Errors like: Limit of total fields \[1000\] has been exceeded )

#### Examples

[](#examples-4)

You would want to prevent ACF fields with names ‘acf\_field\_name1’, ‘acf\_field\_name2’, ‘acf\_field\_name3’ are not indexed.

```
add_filter( 'wpe_smartsearch/acf/excluded_field_names', function ( $excluded_field_names ) {    $custom_excluded_field_names= array(       'acf_field_name1',       'acf_field_name2',       'acf_field_name3',    );
    return array_merge($excluded_field_names,$custom_excluded_field_names );   }, 10, 1);
```

### `wpe_smartsearch/allow_post_content_filtering`

[](#wpe_smartsearchallow_post_content_filtering)

Allow post content filtering before it is indexed by WP Engine Smart Search.

```
  $allow_post_content_filtering    = apply_filters( 'wpe_smartsearch/allow_post_content_filtering', true );
  if ( $allow_post_content_filtering ) {    $post_array['post_content'] = handle_tags( $post_array['post_content'] );  }
```

#### Description

[](#description-5)

This filter enables or disables the default content stripping before it is indexed. By default, WP Engine Smart Search strips all HTML tags, shortcodes, and block editor comments from the content via the handle\_tags function.

You can use this filter to disable the default content stripping. This is useful if you want to:

-   Preserve certain HTML tags or implement your own content cleaning logic.
-   Use a custom content processing function, as the default stripping might be memory-intensive for very large post content
-   Custom post content processing function can be implemented by using the `wpe_smartsearch/extra_fields` filter.

Note

This filter is enabled by default. If you encounter indexing issues, such as out-of-memory errors, it may indicate that your hosting plan needs an upgrade to handle the higher memory requirements for processing large posts.

#### Examples

[](#examples-5)

You want to prevent the default HTML stripping for all posts to preserve the HTML structure in the search index.

```
    add_filter(      'wpe_smartsearch/allow_post_content_filtering',      '__return_false'    );
```

### `wpe_aitk/enable_search`

[](#wpe_aitkenable_search)

Controls whether Smart Search is enabled for a query.

```
apply_filters( 'wpe_aitk/enable_search', bool $enabled, WP_Query $query )
```

#### Description

[](#description-6)

Smart Search is enabled by default for all standard search queries. When WooCommerce support is active, this is also the standard for product queries.

If a specific scenario requires a different approach, you can use this filter to disable the feature. This is particularly useful for certain post types, categories, or custom queries where you might prefer to use the native search functionality within WordPress.

#### Parameters

[](#parameters-2)

```
$enabled bool
```

Whether Smart Search is enabled for the query. Default is `true`.

```
$query WP_Query
```

The current WP\_Query object being processed.

#### Examples

[](#examples-6)

Disable Smart Search for all queries.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_aitk/enable_search',    '__return_false');
```

Disable Smart Search only for specific post types.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_aitk/enable_search',    function( $enabled, $query ) {        // Disable Smart Search for the 'product' post type        if ( isset( $query->query_vars['post_type'] ) && $query->query_vars['post_type'] === 'product' ) {            return false;        }
        return $enabled;    },    10,    2);
```

Disable Smart Search for WooCommerce product queries on specific pages.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_aitk/enable_search',    function( $enabled, $query ) {        // Disable on the shop page only        if ( is_shop() ) {            return false;        }
        return $enabled;    },    10,    2);
```

Disable Smart Search based on custom query variables.

```
add_filter(    'wpe_aitk/enable_search',    function( $enabled, $query ) {        // Disable for queries with a custom flag        if ( isset( $query->query_vars['use_native_search'] ) && $query->query_vars['use_native_search'] ) {            return false;        }
        return $enabled;    },    10,    2);
```

name: Multisite Setup for WP Engine Smart Search plugin
markdown:
Currently, the WPE Smart Search plugin is not properly configured for multisite installations. We need to manually set up the WPE Smart Search plugin for multisite by following these steps:

## A. Obtain WPE Smart Search plugin credentials

[](#a-obtain-wpe-smart-search-plugin-credentials)

1.  Log in to Portal and go to the WP Engine Smart Search product [page](https://my.wpengine.com/products/smart_search#/). ![WP Engine Smart Search Portal](/_astro/smart-search-portal.3HUUWFMF_Z2mXOtt.webp)
2.  Identify the associated environment and click the **Show Credentials** button. ![WP Engine Smart Search Show Credentials](/_astro/smart-search-credentials.DI19qUa0_1rEWqe.webp)
3.  Copy the credentials ( `<URL>` and `<ACCESS_TOKEN>`). These will be used in the next steps.

## B. Set up WPE Smart Search plugin for multisite

[](#b-set-up-wpe-smart-search-plugin-for-multisite)

In this step, network-activate the plugin and copy the credentials obtained previously. There are two ways to do this:

-   Using the [WP Admin](#i-wp-admin-setup)
-   Using the [WP CLI](#ii-wp-cli-setup)

### I. WP Admin setup

[](#i-wp-admin-setup)

1.  Log into WP-Admin and navigate to the network admin plugins page ![WP Engine Smart Search Portal](/_astro/as-network-admin.BAOCXLk-_Z1DI0v6.webp)
2.  Network Activate the plugin ![WP Engine Smart Activate Plugin](/_astro/as-network-activate.C-SC-AGa_1cKA7i.webp)
3.  Go back to the network admin dashboard in wp-admin and access **WP Engine Smart Search → Settings** ![WP Engine Smart Settings](/_astro/as-settings.C0tdAATm_ZVf9Dv.webp)
4.  Paste the credentials from portal and save the configuration. ![WP Engine Smart Credentials](/_astro/as-plugin-credentials.CAzKq1jA_ZGyhzk.webp) Now we are ready to perform an initial indexing of the multisite. ![WP Engine Smart Index](/_astro/as-plugin-index.B0RufqmJ_ZKlvyJ.webp)

### II. WP CLI setup

[](#ii-wp-cli-setup)

Alternatively, you can use WP CLI to network activate the plugin and set up the credentials for network admin. For accessing WP CLI, you need to have [SSH access](https://wpengine.com/support/ssh-gateway/) to the server.

1.  Network activate the plugin
    
    ```
     wp plugin activate atlas-search --network
    ```
    
2.  Set up the credentials, using the `<URL>` and `<ACCESS_TOKEN>` from the portal.
    
    ```
     wp network meta update 1 wpe_content_engine_option_name '{"url":"<URL>","access_token":"<ACCESS_TOKEN>"}' --format=json
    ```
    

Now we are ready to perform an initial indexing of the multisite.

Caution

The `--reset` flag deletes the index and starts indexing all data from scratch.

```
    wp wpe-smart-search sync-data --reset
```
